chunks: And Nadir the servant narrated, saying:
Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) would place one jawzinja (a sweet) upon the other, and hand it to me.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu Al-Hasan, referring to Imam Ali al-Rida (peace be upon him)
key_terms.جَوْزِينَجَةً: Jawzinja, a type of sweet or confection
key_terms.نَادِرٌ: Nadir, a specific narrator known as 'the servant'

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Abu Al-Hasan do with sweets for his servant Nadir?
ai.summary: This brief narration from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the humility and approachability of Imam Ali al-Rida (peace be upon him), demonstrating that spiritual leadership does not preclude enjoying simple worldly pleasures. By personally stacking and handing over the *jawzinja* (a walnut-based sweet), the Imam models graciousness and breaks down social barriers between the Imams and their companions, reinforcing the Shia concept of the Imam as both a spiritual guide and a relatable human figure.
